prompt.context: Our client, Shermer Pharma, is a venture-backed start-up pharmaceutical company. Over the past 15 years, Shermer has been developing a molecule that has been approved by the FDA to cure Alzheimer's with 90% efficacy. Shermer currently has no Sales or Marketing organization — the company has purely been a research firm to this point. FDA approval has been granted.
prompt.question: Shermer's owners have hired us to answer two questions: (1) How should we sell our product? (2) Is our product going to be profitable?

clarifying_info.a: A pill that cures Alzheimer's disease — an illness that currently has no treatment that cures or stops the progress of the disease.
A degenerative, terminal disease that causes senility and dementia. Approximately 30 million people suffer from it worldwide.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the target customers / buyers?
clarifying_info.a: Sales would be focused on neurologists and geriatric psychiatrists, not the consumer of the product.

clarifying_info.q: Does Shermer have any existing sales or marketing capabilities?
clarifying_info.a: No. The company has purely been a research firm; there is no existing Sales or Marketing organization.

clarifying_info.q: Are there competitors with a similar product?
clarifying_info.a: No. Shermer will be the only firm with a cure for this illness for the next 5 years — we will not focus on competitive response during this case.

clarifying_info.q: What is the size of the Alzheimer's market?
clarifying_info.a: Try to size it yourself first; the actual answer is 5 million patients (in the addressable/treatment market).
We can ignore taxes for this analysis.
We can ignore NPV and assume straight-line amortization of R&D costs.

clarifying_info.q: What is the requirement for recovering R&D costs?
clarifying_info.a: The firm requires that R&D costs be recovered by Year 5 of the product launch.

exhibits.title: Sales Force Options
exhibits.shows: A comparison table of two sales force models — Develop Own Sales Force vs. Contract Sales Force — with rows for: percent of visit focused on our product, fully loaded annual cost of one sales rep, cost per sales call, total calls required, total sales reps needed, and total annual selling cost. Several cells are intentionally left blank for the candidate to calculate.

exhibits.title: Annual Net Income
exhibits.shows: A five-year P&L table with rows for: projected market penetration (%), total users, total gross margin, amortized R&D costs, selling costs, G&A costs, and net income. The penetration percentages are given; all dollar rows are blank for the candidate to fill in. Key data provided separately as the candidate asks: total market = 5MM, annual gross margin per user = $1,000, R&D cost = $1.5B, G&A cost = $25MM per year.

framework: Clarify the product and market context (what disease, who buys, competitive landscape, existing capabilities)
Size the Alzheimer's market (bottom-up estimate, then confirm with provided figure of 5MM patients)
Analyze go-to-market / sales channel options: (1) Build own internal sales force, (2) Contract sales organization, (3) Sell the company to a larger pharma firm
Evaluate each option financially using Exhibit 1 (sales force costs) — calculate missing cells
Build a 5-year P&L using Exhibit 2 — determine profitability and whether R&D is recovered by Year 5
Synthesize: recommend sales channel and confirm overall profitability

questions.prompt: Part 1 — Sales Channel: Using Exhibit 1, calculate the missing figures and determine which sales force option is cheaper.
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize that contract reps only spend 50% of their time on Shermer's product, so twice as many calls and reps are needed. They should calculate cost per call for the own sales force, total calls and reps for contract, and total annual selling cost for both. Contract sales ($12MM/yr) is cheaper than own sales force ($17MM/yr).

math.setup:
Own Sales Force: Fully loaded cost per rep = $200k; each rep makes 1,000 calls/year; 85% of time on calls → calls per rep = 85k/100 = 850... simpler: cost per call = $200k * (85/100) / 1000 calls? The casebook derives: cost per call = ($200k * 85) / 100k calls = $170. Total calls required = 100k (given). Total reps = 85 (given). Total annual selling cost = $200k * 85 = $17MM.

Contract Sales Force: cost per call = $60 (given). Because reps spend only 50% of time on Shermer, twice as many calls are needed: total calls = 100k * 2 = 200k. Total reps = 85 * 2 = 170. Total annual selling cost = $60 * 200k = $12MM.
steps: Own SF total selling cost: $200k × 85 reps = $17MM
Contract SF total calls needed: 100k × 2 = 200k (because only 50% focus)
math.answer: Contract sales force total annual cost = $12MM; Own sales force = $17MM. Contract sales is $5MM cheaper per year.

questions.prompt: Market Sizing Brain Teaser (optional step): Estimate the size of the US/global Alzheimer's patient market.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a bottom-up estimate (e.g., US population ~330MM, ~13% over 65, ~10% of those have Alzheimer's → ~4–5MM in US). Interviewer provides the answer of 5MM at the end of the exercise.

math.setup: Bottom-up: US population ≈ 330MM. ~13% aged 65+ ≈ 43MM. ~10–12% of 65+ have Alzheimer's ≈ 4.3–5.2MM.

questions.prompt: Part 2 — Profitability: Using Exhibit 2, build the 5-year P&L and determine if R&D costs are recovered by Year 5.
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask for key data (total market, gross margin per user, R&D cost, G&A). They should calculate total users by applying penetration % to 5MM market, compute gross margin, subtract amortized R&D ($1.5B / 5 = $300MM/yr), subtract selling costs ($12MM using contract sales), subtract G&A ($25MM). Net income is negative in Year 1 but cumulative profitability is achieved and R&D is recovered by Year 5.

math.setup: Total market = 5MM. Gross margin per user per year = $1,000. R&D cost = $1.5B amortized straight-line over 5 years = $300MM/yr. Selling costs (contract) = $12MM/yr. G&A = $25MM/yr. Penetration: Y1=5%, Y2=10%, Y3=25%, Y4=40%, Y5=60%.
steps: Cumulative 5-year net income = −$87MM + $163MM + $913MM + $1.663B + $2.663B = ~$5.315B > $0; R&D fully recovered.
math.answer: Net income: Y1=−$87MM, Y2=$163MM, Y3=$913MM, Y4=$1.663B, Y5=$2.663B. Product is profitable; R&D cost recovered well before Year 5 on a cumulative basis.

brainstorming.prompt: What else should be considered before engaging this plan? (High-level analysis at the end of the case)

categories.name: Sales channel considerations
ideas: Effectiveness of contract sales vs. own sales force — contract reps are typically less effective since they split focus
For only $5MM more per year, an own sales force may deliver better outcomes given revenues of $3B+
Third option: sell Shermer to a larger pharma firm with existing sales/marketing infrastructure

categories.name: Pricing
ideas: $1,000/year per patient for a life-saving cure for a currently incurable disease is likely significantly underpriced
Pricing power is high given no competition for 5 years and 90% efficacy
Should explore value-based pricing or higher price tiers

categories.name: Competitive dynamics
ideas: No competitors for 5 years — but must plan for competitive entry at Year 5+
Pipeline: can R&D capabilities be redirected to develop next-generation treatments?

categories.name: Organizational build-out
ideas: Need to hire marketing, sales management, and support staff even with contract sales
KOL (key opinion leader) engagement with neurologists and geriatric psychiatrists

categories.name: Market access and reimbursement
ideas: Insurance/payer reimbursement approval is critical for patient access
Government reimbursement (Medicare/Medicaid) given elderly patient population

categories.name: Manufacturing and supply chain
ideas: Scale-up of manufacturing to meet projected demand (1.25MM+ users by Year 3)
Quality control and regulatory compliance for commercial-scale production

recommendation: Shermer Pharma should go to market via a contract sales organization, as it is the lower-cost option ($12MM vs. $17MM/yr) and better suited to a company whose core competency is research, not sales and marketing.

An alternative worth exploring is selling the company to a larger pharmaceutical firm with existing commercial infrastructure — this would maximize value for the venture-backed owners and eliminate execution risk.
The product is financially viable: the P&L shows losses only in Year 1, with strong profitability from Year 2 onward and full R&D cost recovery well within the 5-year window.
risks: Contract sales force may be less effective than own sales force, potentially reducing market penetration rates
$1,000/year pricing may be significantly below market value — leaving material revenue on the table
Organizational build-out (even for contract model) requires capabilities Shermer does not currently possess
Competitive entry after Year 5 requires a plan for IP protection and pipeline development
next_steps: Conduct a formal pricing analysis to assess optimal price point given willingness-to-pay and payer dynamics
Evaluate two or three contract sales organizations and negotiate terms, including performance incentives
Engage insurance and government payers early to secure reimbursement approvals before launch
Begin organizational design for the commercial function (marketing, medical affairs, sales management)
Develop a 5-year competitive response plan for post-patent / post-exclusivity entry
